examples.problem: Find the second degree Taylor polynomial of the function $f(x) = e^{2x}$ about $x=1.$
examples.worked_solution:
To find the second-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=1,$ we plug $a=1$ into the general formula to give

$$
P_2(x) = f(1) + f'(1)(x-1) +\dfrac{1}{2}f''(1)(x-1)^2.
$$

So we need to work out $f(1),$ $f'(1),$ and $f''(1)\mathbin{;}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={e}^{2x} & ⟹ &  & f(1) & ={e}^{2} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2{e}^{2x} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(1) & =2{e}^{2} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =4{e}^{2x} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(1) & =4{e}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We now plug the results for $f(1),$ $f'(1),$ and $f''(1)$ into our second-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & ={e}^{2}+2{e}^{2}(x-1)+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4{e}^{2}(x-1)^{2} \\  & ={e}^{2}+2{e}^{2}(x-1)+2{e}^{2}(x-1)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
